readerContract.humanQuestion: Why are people arguing over the pace of AI, and does the September 13 debate change what is checked now?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Understand the disagreement over pace and independent checking without mistaking a statement or company proposal for a new rule.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: A reader may hear “guardrails” and assume a new rule has arrived.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: The disagreement is about whether speed should yield time for safety work and who can independently check it; remarks and proposals do not themselves change a reader’s tools.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A reader who sees “AI guardrails” in the news can tell a company commitment from a government action before assuming her AI tool changed.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A short dated September 13 NewsStand explanation of reported remarks and their limit.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I know what this story says happened, what did not happen in the report, and what evidence to seek next.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Trump argued for maintaining the U.S. AI lead while Amodei argues that safety work needs more time and independent checking; neither source establishes a new federal rule.
causalSequence: Calls to slow development ask for time to test and check safety work.
Trump’s reported response prioritizes staying ahead in the AI race while acknowledging some regulation.
Amodei’s concrete proposal is external evaluators; it remains a company proposal and commitment.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: The reported disagreement gives a reader two distinct positions—speed and external checking—without claiming either is law.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: For another policy debate, ask what the proposed check is and whether it is a company commitment or named government action.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Ask who would check the safety work and what form of action is actually named.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; Class Notes.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Use only the AP report; do not revive inaccessible Axios material, speculative policy outcomes or a national no-safeguards claim.

explanationArc.adaptation: A brief policy explainer, not a legal survey or legislative forecast.

discoveryChecks.question: Did OpenAI create mandatory national rules?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. OpenAI asked Congress to enact them.

discoveryChecks.question: Did Sanders and Casar’s announcement establish an AI pause?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. Their office described the legislation as forthcoming.

discoveryChecks.question: Are the proposals the same?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. OpenAI proposes targeted capability-based duties for the largest labs; Sanders and Casar propose a pause until a regulator sets rules plus a permanent ban on their defined category of superintelligence.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Turning AP’s reported lack of specifics into an unsupported national absence claim.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Every factual sentence maps to the AP capture; the article says only that AP did not identify a concrete step, not that none exists.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: Reader can state the difference between remarks, a meeting and a named action.
